source: Hook et al. (2022), Economic Burden of Reported Lyme Disease in High-Incidence Areas, United States, 2014–2016
verification: Checked user-supplied public article text: Methods, Results and Discussion. Linked tables not separately retrieved. Live website blocked.
limitations: Quota-sampled reported confirmed/probable cases in four high-incidence states; recruitment September 2014–January 2016
Patient costs include productivity losses; not synonymous with out-of-pocket payments
Societal total includes medical, nonmedical and productivity costs; do not add them again
Excluded non-English speakers; 94% of study participants were white; not a population risk estimate
Excluded suspected, undiagnosed and nonacute disease; does not value persistent long-term symptoms
Monthly surveys ended after two without expenses or a maximum of twelve; not a lifetime total
Recall, billing attribution and surveillance weighting may bias costs
Different disease groups do not prove effects of diagnostic delay or intervention savings
National mean/median illustrations are not a confidence interval; local extrapolation requires explicit assumptions
